DATABASE_URL

One connection string, encoding everything Prisma needs to find and log into the database.

Everything Prisma needs to know to reach MySQL — who to log in as, what password, which host and port, which database — gets encoded into a single connection string, read from .env the same way PORT was in Week 1.

# Figure 2.2: the new setting (.env.example, excerpt)
DATABASE_URL="mysql://root:root@localhost:3306/support_desk"

Reading it left to right: mysql:// (which database engine to speak), root:root (username:password), @localhost:3306 (host:port), and /support_desk (the database name) — matching the root password, port, and database name set in docker-compose.yml on the previous slide exactly. Point this at a differently-configured MySQL (a different port, a real password, a managed cloud instance later on) and only this one line changes — nothing in schema.prisma or the application code ever hardcodes a host or password.

As with PORT, .env itself is never committed (it's where the real value lives for your machine); .env.example documents the shape every developer's .env needs, with placeholder credentials that happen to match this project's own docker-compose.yml for convenience.
